links.comparator_used: Same pathologist's unassisted reading (reference standard); AI alone was run as a separate step but not scored against the AI-assisted reading
links.outcome: Gleason/grade group assessment, tumor detection agreement, and diagnostic confidence with vs without AI assistance
links.effect: GG assessments differed in 16.5% (30/182) of entries; 80.0% (24/30) were one-point changes and 20.0% (6/30) two-point changes; 36.7% (11/30) of discrepancies were shifts between GG1 and GG2; tumor detection agreement 98.6% (279/283), with differences limited to GG1 tumors; confidence rose from confident to high confidence
links.tradeoff: AI assistance altered grading in a sizeable minority of cases, including clinically relevant GG1/GG2 shifts; accuracy against an independent truth was not established because the unassisted pathologist was the reference
links.quote: In clinical practice, AI assistance influenced Gleason grading in 16.5% of entries.

design_hint: AI-assisted pathologist review of biopsies compared with unassisted reading
